authority.non_authority_statement: This active inventory grants no accepted-decision, implementation, or activation authority.

lifecycle.terminal_handling: Remove resolved, rejected, or superseded records in the same bounded package that records their accepted ADR, canonical rationale, or explicit rejection; preserve history in Git and linked Issues rather than in a second permanent archive.

records.blocking_owner_question: Does the repository owner approve automatic deletion of merged ephemeral PR branches with explicit protected, release, rollback, active-claim, and recovery exceptions?
records.decision_question: Which lifecycle policy should govern source branches after their pull requests merge?

DERIVED: Automatic deletion with explicit exceptions reduces stale ownership signals without removing recovery-critical branches.
PROVEN: Issue #586 records that delete_branch_on_merge is disabled and terminal merged branches remain unclassified.
UNKNOWN: The repository owner's approved exception set and one-time cleanup policy are not yet selected.

options.description: Enable automatic deletion for ordinary merged PR branches and retain only branches proven to match protected, release, rollback, active-claim, or recovery exceptions.
options.title: Automatic deletion with explicit exceptions
trade_offs: Reduces stale branches but requires a precise exception and recovery policy.

options.description: Keep automatic deletion disabled and require every merged branch to be manually deleted or explicitly classified during closeout.
options.title: Mandatory manual terminal classification
trade_offs: Preserves direct control but retains recurring cleanup and enforcement cost.

options.description: Automatically delete only standardized task and repair branches while retaining other branch classes for manual review.
options.title: Prefix-scoped hybrid policy
trade_offs: Limits automation risk but makes lifecycle depend on naming discipline and leaves more ambiguous branches.

records.problem_statement: Merged source branches accumulate without one canonical deletion, retention, exception, and recovery policy, weakening deterministic task ownership and branch discovery.
records.recommendation: Adopt option A with fail-closed exclusions for protected, release, rollback, active-claim, open-PR, and recovery branches.
records.title: Select merged source-branch lifecycle policy

records.blocking_owner_question: Should Oteryn Platform remain proprietary/no-permission, become source-available under exact owner-selected terms, or adopt an exact open-source license after provenance and compatibility review?
records.decision_question: What legal distribution and contribution-rights model governs the public Oteryn Platform repository?

DERIVED: An explicit temporary no-permission boundary is safer than silently granting rights before third-party provenance is reviewed.
PROVEN: Issue #587 records that the public repository has no canonical license, SPDX declaration, or licensing policy.
UNKNOWN: Third-party asset provenance, dependency compatibility, contribution terms, and the owner's selected distribution model remain unresolved.

options.description: Document that public source visibility grants no copying, modification, redistribution, or contribution rights beyond applicable law.
options.title: Proprietary or no-permission policy
trade_offs: Minimizes unintended grants but restricts reuse and external contribution.

options.description: Publish owner-selected source-available terms after legal and provenance review.
options.title: Source-available terms
trade_offs: Permits bounded use but requires custom-term maintenance and compatibility analysis.

options.description: Adopt an exact OSI-approved license and contribution boundary after proving all bundled materials are compatible.
options.title: Open-source license
trade_offs: Maximizes reuse and contribution but may conflict with bundled assets or intended commercial control.

records.problem_statement: The repository is publicly readable but does not define copying, modification, redistribution, contribution, or bundled-asset licensing rights.
records.recommendation: Use option A as the explicit interim boundary until provenance and compatibility review supports an owner-approved broader license.
records.recommended_owner: repository owner with qualified legal review
records.title: Select repository licensing and distribution policy

records.blocking_owner_question: Does the repository owner approve GitHub private vulnerability reporting plus a monitored role-based security contact as the canonical confidential reporting channel?
records.decision_question: Which confidential vulnerability reporting channel, supported-version scope, and response ownership should govern Oteryn Platform?

DERIVED: A private GitHub reporting path plus a role-based contact provides the clearest repository-native route while avoiding public exploit disclosure.
PROVEN: Issue #588 records that no SECURITY.md, confidential reporting channel, or supported-version disclosure policy exists.
UNKNOWN: The private vulnerability reporting setting, monitored security contact, supported versions, and owner-approved response expectations remain unresolved.

options.description: Enable GitHub private vulnerability reporting and publish a role-based security contact and repository scope in SECURITY.md.
options.title: GitHub private reporting plus role contact
trade_offs: Provides repository-native confidential intake but requires administration access and monitored ownership.

options.description: Use only a monitored role-based mailbox or equivalent private contact documented in SECURITY.md.
options.title: Role-based confidential contact
trade_offs: Works independently of GitHub settings but requires separate access control, monitoring, and abuse handling.

options.description: Use a dedicated external vulnerability intake platform and route repository guidance to it.
options.title: External disclosure platform
trade_offs: May improve workflow and coordination but adds vendor, privacy, cost, and availability dependencies.

records.problem_statement: Security researchers have no canonical confidential reporting route, supported-version boundary, or response owner and may disclose sensitive details in public Issues.
records.recommendation: Adopt option A, subject to verification that private vulnerability reporting can be enabled and the role-based contact is actively monitored.
records.title: Select confidential vulnerability disclosure policy
